text:
Aisha (arch): Thinking about cohort probing + feature-flag rollouts without sidecars. Idea: central prober service that tags requests with an opt-in header per-tenant, e.g. X-RW-Compat: probe-v1, and we use runtime routing to route to fallback models or shims. Pros: no sidecar deploys; cons: central control plane complexity and potential latency. Thoughts?
Ken (eng-infra): curious about enforcement paths — if we rely on header, how do we prevent client spoofing? maybe sign the header or mint short-lived tokens?
Priya (eng-platform): we already have short-lived tenant tokens from auth svc. We could HMAC the header using tenant secret. simple: `X-RW-Compat: probe-v1:signature`
Luca (eng-runtime): latency impact? adding HMAC verify on path that is in hot path could add CPU. can we validate in edge LB or as a prefilter in envoy?
Aisha (arch): yep, validate in edge is cleaner. Envoy filter can check HMAC and attach metadata. That keeps runtime lighter. Also TTL cache of prober decisions to avoid checking per-request.
Priya (eng-platform): for private deployments (VPC/on-prem) we can't rely on our envoy changes. fallback: a prober webhook per-customer that the runtime can call for opt-in status.
Ken (eng-infra): noted. Prober webhook means more network calls. we should add local caching with TTL + jittered refresh.
Luca (eng-runtime): KV cache invalidation question: if we route a tenant to a shimmed model variant, we need to flush prefix caches or isolate KV namespaces. Otherwise cached embeddings could be wrong.
Priya (eng-platform): agree. Plan: add per-tenant cache namespace plus a 'probe-version' tag. Invalidate on change. Implementation detail: `cache_key = tenant + ':' + probe_version + ':' + key`
Aisha (arch): sample curl for testing:
```
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
     -H \"X-RW-Compat: probe-v1:abcd1234sig\" \
     https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
Priya (eng-platform): telemetry: tag traces/spans with `compat.probe=probe-v1` and expose metric `requests_compat_probe{probe=\"v1\"}` for rollout health.
Ken (eng-infra): we should also add a `compat_probe_prober_latency` SLI and alert on >250ms median in the first 5m after rollout.
Luca (eng-runtime): concern: canary burst — will prober cause hotspot on a specific pool? need to distribute by region/queue. maybe randomize hash of tenant to spread load.
Aisha (arch): agreed. rollout plan: 1) internal tenant test 2) <1% random tenants for 24h 3) cohort by customer size 4) ramp to 100% with monitoring gates. fallback: automatic rollback on error rate spike.
Priya (eng-platform): action items: implement envoy HMAC filter (Ken), prober service + webhook API (Priya), runtime cache namespacing + probe tag (Luca), telemetry + dashboard (Aisha). I'll create tickets.
Ken (eng-infra): I'll prototype HMAC filter in a small branch. ping @deploy-bot when ready for infra tests.
deploy-bot: CI job #8891 queued for branch `envoy-probe-filter`. Logs: https://ci.redwood/8891 :white_check_mark: 
Luca (eng-runtime): should we add a 'manual override' admin UI for support to opt a tenant in/out? sometimes SRE needs instant fallback.
Aisha (arch): yes, admin override is required. make it an auditable action with an audit log entry.
Priya (eng-platform): final note: for private customers, document the option to deploy a local prober or enable header-signing via their KMS. include in private-deploy checklist.
Aisha (arch): cool — meeting sync next week to review prototypes. thanks all :rocket:
